item.text: The existing 49 tests still pass with the engine wired into verified chat. Marks now start private and pending. I’ve capped retained sessions, marks, and block lists, added a document-size guard, and kept spent slots consumed after veto or forgetting. Forgetting removes the user’s mark data and cooldown identity; a short anonymous channel-wide hold prevents immediate quota bypass.

anchor='## Store and architecture\\n'
section='''## Must milestone: marks backend and original runes

This increment adds the backend engine/store integration only. The Atlas and overlay remain static. There are no public mark mutation, moderation, pending-text, or projection HTTP endpoints. All service methods are internal trusted interfaces; do not expose them to request-supplied actor objects.

**Fail-closed context:** "'`app.marks.setKeeperContext(hostId, { streamId, keeperId, optedIn, holdsRelic, blockedUserIds })` requires an explicit authoritative session ID, numeric Keeper ID, boolean consent/ownership, and a bounded configured blocked-user list. Acceptance requires that the Keeper ID equals the signed chat broadcaster, consent is true and the Keeper holds the relic. Only a trusted lifecycle/ownership integration may call this method. Tests inject synthetic trusted contexts; live stream lifecycle and ownership/opt-in synchronization are **not wired yet**. Runtime startup supplies no context, so real marks remain disabled. No ID is inferred from dates, raid events, names or viewer text. Restoring the same retained stream ID preserves its spent quota.

`!mark word` or `!mark emoji` submits a mark through the already authenticated `channel.chat.message` boundary. Inputs receive Unicode NFKC, locale-independent lowercase and explicit sharp-S/final-sigma folding. The bounded conservative policy accepts one letters/combining-marks word or one supported emoji grapheme (including ZWJ families, modifiers, flags and keycaps). It rejects spaces, control/bidi/invisible word characters, HTML/link syntax and a small substring blocklist. Input is capped at 128 UTF-8 bytes and 32 normalized code points. The filter is intentionally conservative, can reject benign text, and is not comprehensive multilingual abuse/confusable moderation; moderator approval is still required.

`runeSvg(text)` hashes a versioned normalized value into original numeric line/diamond geometry and a fixed palette. No text interpolation, fonts, scripts, external assets or user IDs occur in SVG. Equivalent normalized input yields identical geometry. Pending marks and even their runes stay private until approval. `publicProjection(host)` returns only approved `{ id, runeSvg }` entries for the current eligible stream, with no mark text, user IDs, identity hashes/pseudonyms, timestamps or pending entries. `moderationView(host, actor)` is private and checks trusted moderator identity. No browser rendering/overlay validation is claimed.

**Atomic quotas:** one accepted mark per user per 30 seconds in the configured Keeper channel, across stream transitions; five accepted marks total per broadcaster stream. The application currently supports one configured streamer. Distinct events, retries and concurrency share the same transactional event-dedupe + cooldown + spent-slot + mark mutation. Memory executes the same pure reducer synchronously; Firestore reads all required documents before writing in one transaction. Rejected submissions are acknowledged/deduplicated without spending a slot. Veto, block, opt-out and forgetting never refund spent slots. Changing to a genuinely new authoritative stream creates a fresh five-slot budget; replaying a retained session ID cannot reset it.

Trusted services are `approve(host, actor, markId)`, `vetoLast(host, actor)`, `pause(host, actor, paused)`, `blockUser(host, actor, userId)`, `optOut(host, actor)` and self-only `forgetMe(host, actor)`. Signed chat commands are:

- `!relic approve m1` and `!relic veto-last`.
- `!relic pause` / `!relic resume` to stop/resume mark intake.
- `!relic block <numeric-user-id>` to exclude a user and remove their retained marks.
- `!relic opt-out` to disable intake/public projection and clear retained marks; re-entry requires an explicit trusted consent/context update.
- `!relic forgetme` with **no target argument**, using only the authenticated EventSub chatter identity.

All commands except self-forget require the signed broadcaster'"'s own user ID or the signed event's "'`moderator` badge with ID `1`. Message text, fragments, VIP badges, or claimed role strings confer no authority. Repeated signed command delivery is deduplicated too. Service callers are trusted code and must supply only identities obtained from authenticated sources; there is no application admin login/API in this milestone.

Configured channel blocked users and local moderation blocks are enforced before intake and approval/public projection. Channel bans are **not automatically synchronized**; the future lifecycle/ban integration must populate `blockedUserIds`. No additional OAuth scopes or live ban checks were added. The small blocklist is not a replacement for channel bans or human moderation.

Self-forget removes that chatter'"'s retained pending/approved marks across all retained streams, their stored mark text/association, cooldown identity, and their latest ordinary-chat receipt if still present. There are no separate mark pseudonyms. Only anonymous spent counters/event expiry records remain from those marks; an anonymous 30-second channel-wide hold prevents immediate cooldown bypass without retaining a forgotten identity. Other users are also held briefly during that interval. The chatter can submit new data after that hold. Independently configured channel/moderation safety block lists and OAuth/configuration data are not erased by mark forgetting. This removes retained application mark data in the configured channel; it does **not** erase Twitch chat, logs/backups held elsewhere, or all personal data everywhere.

**Hard storage bounds:** each channel document retains at most 16 explicit stream sessions, each with at most five mark slots, two block lists capped at 128 numeric IDs each, at most 128 short-lived cooldown entries, and a 128 KiB serialized-document guard. IDs/text are length-bounded; this keeps the bounded ledger far below Firestore's 1 MiB document limit. At capacity, new sessions/blocks fail closed rather than silently dropping quotas or safety policy. Retention cleanup and archival expansion are pending; a 17th retained session requires a future reviewed retention policy. This per-channel ledger intentionally trades throughput for simple atomicity at prototype scale. No raw chat command text, actor identity, or pending mark text is written into event dedupe documents or public output.

Tests cover normalization, unsafe inputs, original rune determinism, missing/mismatched context, cooldown boundaries, concurrent five-slot limits and duplicate deliveries, session reuse/reset, moderator authorization, privacy projection, pause/blocks/opt-out, self-forget, command idempotency, bounded documents, and Firestore commit rollback/retry. Firestore tests still use the staged transactional fake; real database/emulator integration remains untested.

'''
s=s.replace(anchor,section+anchor,1)
s=s.replace('and a Firestore adapter tested through injection,', 'and a Firestore adapter tested through injection,',1)
s=s.replace('Curated "'`.codex-evidence/run-NNN.jsonl`'"', 'The Must milestone then added the shared marks reducer, atomic quota/moderation integration, self-forget handling, deterministic original SVG runes and 27 additional mocked tests. Curated "'`.codex-evidence/run-NNN.jsonl`'"',1)
p.write_text(s)
PY"

Implemented the marks backend through verified chat EventSub:

- Unicode-normalized word/emoji filtering and deterministic original SVG runes.
- Atomic dedupe, 30-second user cooldown, and five-mark stream quota in both stores.
- Private pending marks, approved-rune-only public projection, moderation controls, and self-forget.
- Hard storage caps and fail-closed stream/Keeper checks.

**All 76 tests pass**, retaining the previous 49. README and AGENTS are updated.

Live lifecycle context, ban synchronization, real database validation, and overlay work remain pending. Forgetting uses a brief anonymous channel-wide hold to preserve cooldown enforcement.

No credentials read, live/cloud actions, server startup, commits, or other threads.
